description: Adoro te devote enters the prayers: 28 provenance rows per language, five uses, five witnesses and one collation in the bibliography graph, eight new lexicon cards with one changed Polish and one added English sense of sapio, the manifest entry and title in both languages, eight lemmata, two morphology registry rows and the text registry row.

locator.section: Gratiarum actio post Missam; Rhythmus S. Thomae Aquinatis; right column, seven strophes and Amen

insert.claim: Prints the complete seven-strophe Rhythmus S. Thomae Aquinatis with its closing Amen among the thanksgiving prayers after Mass. This page controls the selected letters, accents, capitals and punctuation of all 149 words; the heading and indulgence grant are not part of the text.
insert.decision_reason: Direct reading of the page image of the approved 1962 print. Print authority is not scan-rights clearance; witness review remains separate.

insert.claim: Prints the complete hymn under n. 166 with Amen, in unaccented type with ae digraphs; every one of the 149 selected words stands in the same order.
insert.decision_reason: Direct reading of both page images. The indulgence grant and attribution are not part of the claim.

locator.section: In Honour of the Blessed Sacrament, no. 5, Hymn of S. Thomas Aquinas

insert.claim: Prints the complete hymn with Amen, the first strophe under chant notation and the other six as text; every one of the 149 selected words stands in the same order, with j spellings.
insert.decision_reason: Direct reading of both page images in the current Internet Archive PDF. Chant notation is outside the claim.

locator.section: n. 106, Hymn of St Thomas Aquinas; Latin column

insert.claim: The Latin column prints the complete hymn with Amen. It agrees with the selected text in every word except the accusative Jesum for the vocative Iesu at the head of the last strophe, and spells pelicane and pœnitens.
insert.decision_reason: Direct reading of the Latin column on all three page images. The parallel English column is not part of this neutral Latin claim.

locator.section: Gratiarum actio post Missam; Rhythmus S. Thomae Aquinatis; right column, seven strophes ending Amen

insert.claim: This separately set manifestation prints the same 149 words in the same order. It spells súbicit and pelicáne, capitalizes Sánguine, sets a comma after intúeor and a semicolon after sítio, and prints Amen on the last verse line. It corroborates one received tradition, not independent historical transmission.
insert.decision_reason: Direct reading of the page image of the separately set typical-edition page. No scan redistribution or independent ancestry is claimed.

insert.independence_basis: Direct page-image transcription of the Benziger 1962 setting; the Vatican setting is a separate manifestation of the same official tradition, not independent historical transmission.
Direct page-image transcription of the 1952 Enchiridion; not derived from another retained witness.
Direct page-image transcription of the 1961 Liber Usualis; not derived from another retained witness.
Direct page-image transcription of the Latin column of the 1910 Raccolta; not derived from another retained witness.
Direct page-image transcription of the separately set Vatican typical-edition page; same official tradition as the Benziger setting, not independent historical transmission.

insert.recension: Complete Rhythmus of the 1962 Missal thanksgiving after Mass, selected from the Benziger setting and compared with the Vatican setting, the 1952 Enchiridion, the 1961 Liber Usualis and the 1910 Raccolta
